title: Binary soft-code encode: can Hamming (XOR/popcount) preserve the frozen random-3072 accuracy at a fraction of the float cdist encode cost?

device._note: M114's binary encode is CPU-native (XOR + POPCNT, single instructions) and needs NO GPU cdist; whitening, hashing, Hamming and ridge all run on numpy CPU. The GPU is only exercised by the parity guard. HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1, gfx1201.

parity_guard.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens

sparse.random_dictionary: M108/M113 arm (a) exact: prefix of the seeded permutation of the shared 8192-whitened-patch pool - IDENTICAL to the dictionary M113 measured at 0.2153
sparse.hash_learned: ITQ (Gong et al., CVPR 2011): PCA top-B on the whitened-patch pool, random orthogonal rotation, 50 alternation iterations; code = sign((x - center) @ P - bias). B is capped at 108 = PATCH_DIM: a linear projection of the 108-dim whitened patch has at most 108 informative bits
sparse.hash_control: seeded Gaussian projection (unit-norm columns), same pool and bias convention - isolates whether hash LEARNING matters
sparse.hamming: packed uint64 XOR + POPCNT (numpy bitwise_count, hardware POPCNT instruction); triangle kernel on Hamming distances, soft assignment over ALL atoms (never truncated - M113 arm (c) showed truncation destroys the soft code)

head._note: M108's chosen head constant, applied unchanged.

gate.float_reference: QUOTED from M113 sealed random-3072 = 0.2153 @ 254.6M MACs (M113 re-measured M108's at delta +0.00000 on 6 Aug; this run rebuilds the IDENTICAL deterministic dictionary)
gate.kill_switch_1_hash_learning: if binary ITQ-256 does not beat binary RANDOM-256 by >= +0.01, hash learning adds nothing over random bits
gate.kill_switch_2_mac_axis_breakthrough: if binary ITQ-256 < float(0.2153) - 0.01 OR its total ops > float total MACs / 3, no MAC-axis win is licensed; if BOTH pass, the sparse family wins the MAC axis at preserved accuracy - the first measured time
gate.registered_prediction: the Hamming triangle preserves the soft assignment's coarse geometry (unlike top-k truncation), so a modest accuracy drop is expected, but within 0.01 of float is the open question; the cost win (~5-8x) is structural and should hold
